hints: Start by picturing butanone clearly, it is the ketone $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, so ask what ketones can and cannot do.
Remember that $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces the $\text{C=O}$ of a ketone to $\text{CH-OH}$, so work out the structure of butan-2-ol formed here.
Check that alcohol product for a carbon with four different groups, that chiral centre is the key to spotting the correct statement.
walkthrough:
**Identify butanone**

Think ketone, not alcohol and not aldehyde. Its structure is:

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

This one $\text{C=O}$ in the middle controls all its reactions.

**Rule out the impossible reactions**

Dehydration with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is a reaction of alcohols (loss of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to form an alkene). Butanone has no $\text{-OH}$ to lose, so A is impossible.

Tollens' reagent oxidises aldehydes to carboxylates, but ketones resist oxidation, so no silver mirror forms and B is wrong.

**Check the mechanism with HCN**

Aldehydes and ketones react with HCN by nucleophilic addition, because $\text{CN}^-$ attacks the slightly positive carbonyl carbon.

$$\text{C=O + CN}^- \rightarrow \text{C(CN)-O}^-$$

It is nucleophilic, not electrophilic, so C is wrong.

**Confirm reduction with NaBH4**

$\text{NaBH}_4$ is a reducing agent that adds hydride ($\text{H}^-$) to the carbonyl carbon to give a secondary alcohol:

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + 2[\text{H}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

The product is butan-2-ol. Carbon-2 is bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, four different groups, so it is chiral. This makes D correct.

options.A: False. Dehydration (loss of water to give an alkene) is characteristic of alcohols with concentrated H2SO4, not ketones. Butanone has no OH group to eliminate, so it cannot give CH2=CHCH=CH2 this way.
options.B: False. Tollens' reagent gives a positive silver mirror only with aldehydes, which are easily oxidised. Ketones like butanone are not oxidised under these mild conditions, so the test stays negative.
options.C: False. Addition of HCN to a carbonyl is initiated by the nucleophile CN- attacking the delta-positive carbon. It is a classic example of nucleophilic addition, not electrophilic addition.
options.D: Correct. NaBH4 reduces butanone to butan-2-ol, CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3. The C-2 bearing the OH is attached to four different groups, so the product is chiral (formed as a racemic mixture).
